formula_latex: V = I \times R \quad \& \quad P = V \times I

faqs.q: What is Ohm's Law?
faqs.a: Ohm's Law states that current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to voltage across the points, inversely proportional to resistance.

faqs.q: How to calculate power from voltage and current?
faqs.a: Power in Watts equals Voltage in Volts multiplied by Current in Amperes (P = V × I).

name: LED Series Resistor Calculator
meta_title: LED Series Resistor Calculator - Current Limiting Resistor & Power
meta_desc: Calculate the exact current-limiting series resistor and power rating for any LED and supply voltage.
summary: Prevent burning out LEDs by finding the exact resistance and recommended standard resistor wattage.

faqs.q: Why does an LED need a series resistor?
faqs.a: LEDs have non-linear forward voltage characteristics. Without a current-limiting resistor, excessive current will burn out the LED.

faqs.q: What is standard forward voltage for blue/white LEDs?
faqs.a: Blue and white LEDs typically have forward voltages between 3.0V and 3.4V, while red LEDs are around 1.8V to 2.2V.

name: Voltage Divider Calculator
meta_title: Voltage Divider Calculator - Output Voltage & Resistor Ratio
meta_desc: Calculate output voltage (Vout) from input voltage (Vin) and resistor values (R1, R2) with transfer ratio.
summary: Quickly design potential dividers for ADC input scaling, level shifting, and reference voltages.

faqs.q: What is the loading effect on a voltage divider?
faqs.a: Connecting a load resistor in parallel with R2 decreases equivalent resistance, dropping Vout. Ensure load impedance is at least 10x higher than R2.

name: Battery Life & Runtime Calculator
meta_title: Battery Life Calculator - Runtime in Hours & Days
meta_desc: Calculate battery life in hours, days, and duty-cycle standby for IoT, robotics, and embedded devices.
summary: Estimate real-world operating time of battery powered systems factoring in discharge derating.

faqs.q: Why apply an 85% discharge factor?
faqs.a: Chemical batteries suffer from self-discharge, voltage sag, and temperature variations, rarely delivering 100% rated capacity.

faqs.q: What is 1 oz copper thickness?
faqs.a: 1 oz copper corresponds to approximately 1.37 mils or 35 micrometers (μm) thickness on a PCB.

meta_desc: Compute frequency, time high, time low, and duty cycle for NE555 timer in astable multivibrator mode.
summary: Design pulse generators, PWM clocks, and LED flashers instantly.

faqs.q: Can a 555 timer generate a 50% duty cycle?
faqs.a: Standard astable 555 duty cycle is always > 50%. A bypass diode across R2 is required for duty cycles <= 50%.

summary: Filter high-frequency noise and smooth PWM signals into analog voltages.

faqs.q: What happens at the cutoff frequency?
faqs.a: At fc, output voltage drops by -3dB (70.7% of input) and experiences a 45° phase lag.

faqs.q: What does 0 dBm equal?
faqs.a: 0 dBm represents exactly 1 milliwatt (1 mW) of power into a 50-ohm reference load.

faqs.q: What is the recommended max voltage drop?
faqs.a: NEC recommends a maximum voltage drop of 3% for branch circuits to ensure device efficiency.

faqs.q: What does SMD code 472 mean?
faqs.a: 472 represents 47 followed by 2 zeros = 4,700 Ohms (4.7 kΩ).

name: Heat Sink Thermal Resistance Calculator
meta_title: Heat Sink Thermal Resistance Calculator | Calculate Required Cooling
meta_desc: Calculate the required thermal resistance for heat sinks to keep your electronic components within safe operating temperatures. Ensure reliable design.
summary: This calculator determines the maximum allowable thermal resistance of a heat sink based on power dissipation and ambient temperature to prevent component overheating.
formula_latex: R_{\theta SA} = \frac{T_{j} - T_{a}}{P_{d}} - R_{\theta JC} - R_{\theta CS}

faqs.q: Why is Rthcs included in thermal calculations?
faqs.a: Rthcs (Case-to-Sink thermal resistance) accounts for the thermal interface material (TIM) or grease between the component and the heat sink, which is critical for accurate calculations.

faqs.q: What happens if the calculated thermal resistance is negative?
faqs.a: A negative result indicates that the power dissipation is too high for the component to operate safely at the given ambient temperature, even without a heat sink.

name: Buck Converter Inductor Sizing Calculator
meta_desc: Calculate the optimal inductor value for your DC-DC buck converter to ensure stable ripple current and efficient power conversion for your IoT projects.
summary: Determines the minimum inductance required for a buck converter based on input/output voltage, switching frequency, and target inductor ripple current.

faqs.q: Why is inductor ripple current important?
faqs.a: Keeping ripple current between 20% and 40% of the maximum output current balances efficiency, physical component size, and output voltage ripple.

faqs.q: What happens if the inductor value is too low?
faqs.a: A low inductance causes higher peak currents, which can lead to inductor saturation, increased switching losses, and higher output voltage noise.

name: Solar IoT & CCTV Autonomy Calculator
meta_title: Solar IoT & CCTV Autonomy Calculator - Battery & Panel Sizing
meta_desc: Calculate the required solar panel wattage and battery capacity for your IoT or CCTV project to ensure 24/7 operation during low-sunlight conditions.
summary: Determines the optimal battery capacity and solar array size needed to maintain continuous power for remote IoT devices based on daily energy consumption and site-specific solar insolation.

faqs.q: How many days of autonomy should I plan for?
faqs.a: For mission-critical CCTV, 3 to 5 days is standard to account for consecutive cloudy days.

faqs.q: Does the system voltage affect battery capacity?
faqs.a: Yes, higher system voltages reduce the total Amp-hour requirement for the same amount of Watt-hours.

name: H-Bridge Power Dissipation Calculator
meta_title: H-Bridge Motor Driver Power Dissipation & Thermal Calculator
meta_desc: Calculate power loss and thermal dissipation for MOSFET-based H-Bridge motor drivers to ensure reliable operation and prevent thermal shutdown.
summary: Calculates power dissipation in H-Bridge motor drivers caused by conduction losses to determine if a heat sink is required for your specific motor load.

faqs.q: Why is it multiplied by 2?
faqs.a: In a standard H-Bridge, current flows through two MOSFETs simultaneously during each phase of the switching cycle.

faqs.q: What happens if dissipation exceeds the package limit?
faqs.a: The MOSFET junction temperature will exceed safe limits, leading to performance degradation or permanent thermal failure.

name: Microstrip Transmission Line Impedance Calculator
meta_title: Microstrip Impedance Calculator | PCB Trace Design Tool
meta_desc: Calculate the characteristic impedance of a microstrip transmission line based on PCB trace width, substrate height, and dielectric constant (Er).
summary: Quickly determine the characteristic impedance of PCB traces for high-speed signal integrity and RF matching.

faqs.q: Why is trace impedance important?
faqs.a: Maintaining consistent impedance prevents signal reflections, which can cause data errors and signal degradation in high-frequency circuits.

faqs.q: Does copper thickness affect impedance?
faqs.a: Yes, increasing copper thickness slightly lowers the characteristic impedance because it increases the effective width of the trace.

name: Solar MPPT Panel Array Sizing Calculator
meta_title: Solar MPPT Array Sizing Calculator | Voltage & Power Config
meta_desc: Calculate the optimal solar panel configuration for your MPPT charge controller based on open-circuit voltage (Voc) and temperature coefficients.
summary: Ensure your solar panel array voltage stays within the safe operating range of your MPPT charge controller while accounting for cold weather voltage spikes.

faqs.q: Why include temperature in the calculation?
faqs.a: Solar panels produce higher voltage in colder temperatures. If you ignore this, you risk exceeding the MPPT input voltage and damaging the controller.

faqs.q: What happens if I exceed the MPPT voltage?
faqs.a: Exceeding the maximum input voltage typically results in immediate failure or permanent damage to the charge controller's input stage.
